title: Portfolio Platform
tagline: This website: a Next.js 3D frontend with an event-driven Go backend
description: A Next.js and React Three Fiber frontend backed by a Go API. Contact messages are stored in PostgreSQL and published to RabbitMQ. A worker sends the emails, with timed retry queues, a dead-letter queue for bad messages and a parking-lot queue for messages that keep failing.
highlights: RabbitMQ topology: retry queues at 5s / 30s / 2m, a DLQ and a parking lot
Publisher confirms and manual acks, so no message is silently lost
Per-IP token-bucket rate limiting, honeypot spam filter, panic-safe goroutines
Runs with zero infra in memory mode; one docker compose up for the full stack

title: Flight Search Aggregator
tagline: Asks every airline supplier at once and returns the best fares, even when some fail
description: A Go service that fans a search out to several suppliers in parallel, merges the answers, removes duplicates and keeps the cheapest fare per flight. Slow or broken suppliers never slow down or break the whole search.
highlights: Fan-out/fan-in with goroutines, channels and per-supplier timeouts
Circuit breaker per supplier and singleflight: 100 identical searches cause 1 fan-out
Redis cache or an O(1) in-memory LRU, chosen at start-up
O(n) hash-map dedupe and a top-K heap, benchmarked against the naive versions

title: Booking Engine
tagline: Seat booking that can never sell the same seat twice
description: A flight seat-booking engine in Go and PostgreSQL. A test proves the point: with naive code 10 of 10 concurrent users were told they won seat 15A; with this engine's row locks exactly 1 of 50 wins, every time.
highlights: SELECT … FOR UPDATE row locks, taken in a fixed order so they can't deadlock
10-minute seat holds that expire through a min-heap scheduler
Idempotency-Key header, so a retried payment replays the first response
Postgres and in-memory stores pass one shared contract test suite

title: Go Microservices
tagline: Three services joined by gRPC and Kafka, deployed to Kubernetes in CI
description: A flight booking system split into booking, inventory and notification services, built around the hard parts: calls that fail, events that get lost or duplicated, and requests you need to follow across processes.
highlights: Saga with compensation and a transactional outbox to Kafka
Idempotent gRPC calls with retries and deadlines
Consumer dedupe by event ID, retry with backoff, then a dead-letter topic
One trace follows a request through HTTP, gRPC and Kafka in Jaeger

title: API Gateway
tagline: One front door that routes, authenticates, rate-limits and balances load
description: A Go gateway for a set of services: it matches each request to a route, checks the caller's JWT, limits how often they may call, spreads load over healthy backends and records metrics for everything.
highlights: Route lookup in a path-segment trie: 260 ns at 1,000 routes vs 18 µs for a linear scan
Distributed token bucket in Redis via an atomic Lua script
Round robin over healthy backends, with active and passive health checks
Prometheus metrics, latency histograms and JSON access logs

title: Fare Drop Alerts
tagline: Tells you by email or Telegram when a route's fare drops below your price
description: Users create alerts; a scheduler decides when each route is due; workers check fares through RabbitMQ and send notifications when a fare drops. 10,000 alerts on 300 routes cost 300 fare calls per round.
highlights: Min-heap scheduler with one job per route, not per alert
Adaptive polling: routes close to departure are checked more often
Retries with backoff, then a dead-letter exchange
Hysteresis and compare-and-set claims, so nobody gets the same alert twice

title: URL Shortener with Analytics
tagline: Short codes that never collide, and click analytics that never slow a redirect
description: The classic system-design question, built properly: codes come from a scrambled counter, redirects rarely touch the database, and clicks stream through Kafka into batched analytics.
highlights: Base62 over a bijective scramble: 200,000 codes, 0 collisions
Bloom filter rejects unknown codes before Redis or Postgres
HyperLogLog counts unique visitors in 1 KB per link
Clicks buffered and sent to Kafka in batches of up to 500

title: Expense Tracker
tagline: Personal finance dashboard with secure JWT auth
description: Track spending by category and month. A Spring Boot API with stateless JWT security serves a dashboard with monthly totals, a category donut, a 6-month trend chart, and add, edit and delete for expenses. Every query is scoped to the logged-in user.
highlights: Fixed critical security bugs: cross-user data access, ADMIN self-registration, token crashes
Monthly summary endpoint: totals, daily average, top category, 6-month trend
MockMvc integration tests run against Postgres in CI

title: Real-time Chat
tagline: Real-time chat rooms with presence and typing indicators
description: Create or join a room and chat live. Spring Boot runs STOMP over WebSocket (SockJS); messages are stored in MongoDB with cursor-paginated history. The React client shows who is online, who is typing, and reconnects on its own.
highlights: Online presence per room, cleaned up when a socket disconnects
Messages in an indexed collection, so rooms never hit MongoDB’s 16 MB limit
Live STOMP-over-SockJS integration test in CI

title: Kumo Fashion Store
tagline: A shop you can actually use, from browsing to checkout
description: Browse, filter and sort products, pick a size and colour, manage your bag and check out with validated delivery details. Cart state uses useReducer and Context, persisted to localStorage, with stock limits enforced.
highlights: Filters live in the URL, so any view can be shared
Cart, checkout with validation, order confirmation
Responsive down to phone size

title: React Components Lab
tagline: 9 accessible UI components in one app
description: Accordion, image slider, tree view, QR generator, star rating, load-more pagination, colour generator, scroll indicator and a persisted theme toggle. Each is written from scratch with hooks and handles keyboard use plus loading and error states.
highlights: Recursive tree with ARIA roles
Abortable useFetch and a useLocalStorage custom hook
QR codes downloadable as PNG through a canvas

title: Smart Vendor
description: Admin, Vendor and User portals with role-based access control and tenant data isolation. Inventory, order processing and vendor analytics modules are being built.
highlights: Role-based access: Admin / Vendor / User
Tenant data isolation
